```ts
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8000"],
    enableStatus: true,
    discovery: { enabled: true },
    uploads: {
      enforceContentType: true,
      limits: {
        maxFiles: 3,
        maxFileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
        maxTotalSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
        minFileSize: 1,
        maxFilenameLength: 128,
      },
      allow: {
        mimeTypes: ["image/png", "image/jpeg", "application/pdf"],
        extensions: [".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".pdf"],
      },
    },
  },
  onBoot: {
    // The first PGlite start on a slow machine can take longer than the 10 second default.
    maxWaitTime: 30_000,
    fn: async (ctx) => {
      await pushSchema();
      ctx.resources?.logger?.info({
        atFunction: "onBoot",
        message: "my-app booted - PGLite schema ready",
      });
      return Ok(null);
    },
  },
});

if (server.nativeRest) {
  const port = server.config.rest?.port ?? 8000;
  Bun.serve({ port, fetch: server.nativeRest.fetch });
  console.log(`\nmy-app listening on http://localhost:${port}\n`);
}
```

The limits mean: at most three files, five megabytes each, ten megabytes in total, names up to 128 characters, and only PNG, JPEG and PDF files with matching extensions.

## 5. Write a client script [#5-write-a-client-script]

Create `client-upload.ts`. It uploads a small PDF, then tries three requests that should fail: an oversized file, a text file and a missing title:

```ts
import { createNileClient } from "@nilejs/client";
import { z } from "zod";

interface DocumentPayloads {
  documents: {
    inspect: { title: string };
  };
}

const inspectResponseSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  filename: z.string(),
  contentType: z.string(),
  size: z.number(),
});

const nile = createNileClient<DocumentPayloads>({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:8000/api",
});

const pdfBytes = new TextEncoder().encode("%PDF-1.4\n% Project brief\n");
const brief = new File([pdfBytes], "brief.pdf", { type: "application/pdf" });

const uploaded = await nile.upload({
  service: "documents",
  action: "inspect",
  files: { document: brief },
  fields: { title: "Project brief" },
});

if (uploaded.isErr) {
  console.error("upload failed:", uploaded.error, JSON.stringify(uploaded.details));
} else {
  const parsed = inspectResponseSchema.parse(uploaded.value);
  console.log("uploaded", parsed.filename, parsed.contentType, parsed.size, parsed.title);
}

const oversized = new File([new Uint8Array(6 * 1024 * 1024)], "large.pdf", {
  type: "application/pdf",
});
const tooLarge = await nile.upload({
  service: "documents",
  action: "inspect",
  files: { document: oversized },
  fields: { title: "Large scan" },
});
console.log("too large isErr:", tooLarge.isErr, tooLarge.isErr ? tooLarge.error : "");
console.log("too large details:", tooLarge.isErr ? JSON.stringify(tooLarge.details) : "");

const textFile = new File(["plain text"], "notes.txt", { type: "text/plain" });
const wrongType = await nile.upload({
  service: "documents",
  action: "inspect",
  files: { document: textFile },
  fields: { title: "Notes" },
});
console.log("wrong type isErr:", wrongType.isErr, wrongType.isErr ? wrongType.error : "");

const missingTitle = await nile.upload({
  service: "documents",
  action: "inspect",
  files: { document: brief },
  fields: {},
});
console.log("missing title isErr:", missingTitle.isErr, missingTitle.isErr ? missingTitle.error : "");
```

## 6. Run the server and the script [#6-run-the-server-and-the-script]

Start the server in one terminal:

```sh
bun run dev
```

In a second terminal, run the script:

```sh
bun run client-upload.ts
```

You should see one line for the accepted upload and one for each refused request:

```text
uploaded brief.pdf application/pdf 25 Project brief
too large isErr: true upload limit exceeded
too large details: {"error_category":"validation","limit":"maxFileSize","max":5242880,"files":[{"name":"large.pdf","size":6291456}]}
wrong type isErr: true file type not allowed
missing title isErr: true A title is required
```

The `details` value tells you which limit failed and which file caused it. Show that information to the person uploading, not the raw message alone.

## 7. Send the request with curl [#7-send-the-request-with-curl]

Create a small PDF file, then send it as form data. The routing fields `intent`, `service` and `action` go in the same form:

```sh
printf '%%PDF-1.4\n' > tiny.pdf
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -F 'intent=execute' -F 'service=documents' -F 'action=inspect' \
  -F 'title=Project brief' -F 'document=@./tiny.pdf;type=application/pdf'
```

You should see the handler's result with HTTP 200:

```json
{"status":true,"message":"Action 'documents.inspect' executed","data":{"title":"Project brief","filename":"tiny.pdf","contentType":"application/pdf","size":9}}
```

Now send the same action as JSON. Nile Js refuses it because the action expects form data:

```sh
curl -s -w "  [HTTP %{http_code}]\n" -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"documents","action":"inspect","payload":{"title":"Brief"}}'
```

You should see HTTP 400 and the expected content type:

```json
{"status":false,"message":"Action 'documents.inspect' expects multipart/form-data. Send the request as form data with its files.","data":{"error_category":"validation","expected":"multipart/form-data","received":"application/json"}}  [HTTP 400]
```

## 8. Type-check [#8-type-check]

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

You should see no output and exit with status 0.

## What the check does not do [#what-the-check-does-not-do]

The limits look at the declared type and the file extension. They do not read the file's bytes. A text file named `fake.png` with the type `image/png` passes, as the curl test below shows if you try it. Check the content in your handler before you trust it.

```sh
printf 'hello' > fake.png
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -F 'intent=execute' -F 'service=documents' -F 'action=inspect' -F 'title=Fake' \
  -F 'document=@./fake.png;type=image/png'
```

This request returns HTTP 200 with `"contentType":"image/png"`.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **`upload limit exceeded` for a small file.** Check `maxTotalSize` and the request body limit. A body larger than `rest.protection.maxBodyBytes` (10 MiB by default) is refused before parsing.
- **`expects multipart/form-data` with HTTP 400.** The request was sent as JSON. Send the request as form data, as in step 7.

## See also [#see-also]

- [File uploads](/guide/features/file-uploads) lists every limit and how each failure is reported.
- [Uploads](/guide/basics/uploads) has the full configuration reference.
- [Frontend client](/guide/basics/client) explains the `upload` method's options.


---

# Examples

Each example starts from the starter project, adds one feature and runs it. Every file is shown in full, so you can copy the result, and each step ends with output you can compare against. The commands assume Bun 1.4.2 or later and a terminal in the project folder.

| Example | What you build | Features used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Tasks API in React](/guide/examples/tasks-react) | A task list and form in a React component that calls the API through `@nilejs/client` | Actions, client Results, CORS |
| [Protected profile](/guide/examples/protected-profile) | A JWT-protected profile action and a role-checked audit action | JWT, `accessControl`, global before hook |
| [File upload](/guide/examples/file-upload) | A document action that accepts a file with size and type limits | Uploads, structured payload, client `upload` |
| [Realtime order updates](/guide/examples/realtime-orders) | Typed order topics, a protected status action and a socket client | Topics, WebSocket policies, socket client |
| [Weekly report](/guide/examples/weekly-report) | A Monday morning report built by a cron job and delivered through a queue | Cron jobs, queues, lifecycle |
| [Rate-limited quote](/guide/examples/rate-limited-quote) | A public price action that allows a short burst per client | Rate limiting |

## Before you start [#before-you-start]

1. Install Bun 1.4.2 or later and check `bun --version`.
2. Create the starter project with `bunx @nilejs/cli new my-app`, then `cd my-app` and `bun install`.
3. Keep one terminal running `bun run dev` while you call the server from a second terminal.

Each example says which files to create or replace. Files that are not mentioned stay as the starter generated them. Stop a running server with Ctrl+C before you run a script that starts its own server on port 8000.


---

# Protected profile

This example protects two actions in the starter project. `account.profile` accepts any signed-in user. `account.audit` requires the `admin` role, and a global before hook enforces that role for every action that lists it. You will sign tokens for two users with a small helper script and send requests with `curl`.

## What you need [#what-you-need]

- The starter project from the [examples overview](/guide/examples), installed with `bun install`.
- Bun can read `.env` files, so the secret stays out of source control.

## 1. Add the token helper package [#1-add-the-token-helper-package]

The helper script signs tokens with `hono/jwt`, which the Nile Js server already uses:

```sh
bun add hono
```

You should see `1 package installed` or a similar line with no errors.

## 2. Add the secret [#2-add-the-secret]

Create `.env` in the project root. Use your own random value of at least 32 characters:

```text
JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-string-of-at-least-32-characters
```

## 3. Read the secret in one place [#3-read-the-secret-in-one-place]

Create `src/config.ts`. It fails at startup when the secret is missing or too short:

```ts
const jwtSecret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;

if (jwtSecret === undefined || jwtSecret.length < 32) {
  throw new Error("JWT_SECRET must be set to at least 32 characters");
}

export const config = {
  jwtSecret: jwtSecret,
};
```

## 4. Enforce the role in a global hook [#4-enforce-the-role-in-a-global-hook]

Create `src/auth/role-hook.ts`. It runs before every action. Protected actions must list roles in `accessControl`, and the signed-in user's `roles` claim must contain every listed role:

```ts
import type { BeforeActionHandler } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Err, Ok, type Result } from "slang-ts";

/** Requires every role listed in a protected action's accessControl. */
export const requireRolesHook: BeforeActionHandler<boolean, string> = ({
  nileContext,
  action,
}): Result<boolean, string> => {
  if (!action.isProtected) {
    return Ok(true);
  }

  const session = nileContext.getSession("rest");
  if (session === undefined) {
    return Err("Sign in to continue");
  }

  const requiredRoles = action.accessControl ?? [];
  if (requiredRoles.length === 0) {
    return Ok(true);
  }

  const roles = session.roles;
  const hasEveryRole =
    Array.isArray(roles) &&
    requiredRoles.every((role) => roles.includes(role));

  if (!hasEveryRole) {
    return Err("Access denied");
  }

  return Ok(true);
};
```

## 5. Add the two actions [#5-add-the-two-actions]

Create `src/services/account/actions/profile.ts`. It is protected, so the server verifies the token before the handler runs. The handler reads the verified identity from the session:

```ts
import { type NileContext, createAction } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Err, Ok } from "slang-ts";
import { z } from "zod";

const profileSchema = z.object({
  includeOrganization: z.boolean().optional().default(false),
});

type ProfileInput = z.infer<typeof profileSchema>;

const profileHandler = (
  input: ProfileInput,
  context?: NileContext<unknown>
) => {
  const session = context?.getSession("rest");
  if (session === undefined) {
    return Err("Sign in to continue");
  }

  return Ok({
    profile: {
      userId: session.userId,
      organizationId: input.includeOrganization
        ? session.organizationId
        : null,
    },
  });
};

export const profileAction = createAction<ProfileInput>({
  name: "profile",
  description: "Read the signed-in user's profile",
  isProtected: true,
  validation: profileSchema,
  handler: profileHandler,
});
```

Create `src/services/account/actions/audit.ts`. It lists `admin` in `accessControl`, so the role hook checks the claim:

```ts
import { createAction } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Ok } from "slang-ts";

const listAuditHandler = () => {
  return Ok({
    entries: [{ event: "profile.viewed", at: "2026-10-23T09:00:00.000Z" }],
  });
};

export const auditAction = createAction({
  name: "audit",
  description: "List audit entries for administrators",
  isProtected: true,
  accessControl: ["admin"],
  handler: listAuditHandler,
});
```

## 6. Register the service [#6-register-the-service]

Replace `src/services/services.config.ts` so the `account` service is registered next to `tasks`:

```ts
import { createServices, type Services } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { auditAction } from "./account/actions/audit";
import { profileAction } from "./account/actions/profile";
import { createTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/create";
import { deleteTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/delete";
import { getTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/get";
import { listTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/list";
import { updateTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/update";

export const services: Services = createServices([
  {
    name: "tasks",
    description: "Task management with CRUD operations",
    meta: { version: "1.0.0" },
    actions: [
      createTaskAction,
      listTaskAction,
      getTaskAction,
      updateTaskAction,
      deleteTaskAction,
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "account",
    description: "Signed-in account operations",
    actions: [profileAction, auditAction],
  },
]);
```

## 7. Connect auth and the hook to the server [#7-connect-auth-and-the-hook-to-the-server]

Replace `src/index.ts`. It adds the `auth` block, the `onBeforeActionHandler` and the JWT secret from `config`:

```ts
import { createLogger, createNileServer } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { Ok, safeTry } from "slang-ts";
import { requireRolesHook } from "@/auth/role-hook";
import { config } from "@/config";
import { db } from "@/db/client";
import { services } from "@/services/services.config";

const logger = createLogger("my-app", {
  mode: "dev",
  chunking: "monthly",
});

/** Push schema to PGLite on boot */
const pushSchema = async () => {
  const result = await safeTry(() =>
    db.execute(sql`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
        id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        title TEXT NOT NULL,
        description TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
        created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
      )
    `)
  );

  if (result.isErr) {
    console.error("[pushSchema] Failed:", result.error);
  }
};

const server = await createNileServer({
  serverName: "my-app",
  runtime: "bun",
  native: true,
  project: { structure: "error" },
  services,
  resources: { logger, database: db },
  auth: { secret: config.jwtSecret, method: "header" },
  onBeforeActionHandler: requireRolesHook,
  rest: {
    baseUrl: "/api",
    host: "localhost",
    port: 8000,
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8000", "http://localhost:5173"],
    enableStatus: true,
    discovery: { enabled: true },
  },
  onBoot: {
    // The first PGlite start on a slow machine can take longer than the 10 second default.
    maxWaitTime: 30_000,
    fn: async (ctx) => {
      await pushSchema();
      ctx.resources?.logger?.info({
        atFunction: "onBoot",
        message: "my-app booted - PGLite schema ready",
      });
      return Ok(null);
    },
  },
});

if (server.nativeRest) {
  const port = server.config.rest?.port ?? 8000;
  Bun.serve({ port, fetch: server.nativeRest.fetch });
  console.log(`\nmy-app listening on http://localhost:${port}\n`);
}
```

## 8. Create the token helper [#8-create-the-token-helper]

Create `scripts/issue-token.ts`. It signs a token for one user. Pass `admin` as the first argument to include the `admin` role:

```ts
import { sign } from "hono/jwt";
import { config } from "../src/config";

type TokenRequest = {
  userId: string;
  organizationId: string;
  roles: string[];
};

const ONE_HOUR_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60;

/** Development helper: prints a signed token for the given identity. */
const issueToken = async (request: TokenRequest): Promise<string> => {
  const expiresAt = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + ONE_HOUR_IN_SECONDS;
  return await sign(
    {
      userId: request.userId,
      organizationId: request.organizationId,
      roles: request.roles,
      exp: expiresAt,
    },
    config.jwtSecret
  );
};

const role = process.argv[2] === "admin" ? ["admin"] : ["member"];
const token = await issueToken({
  userId: "user_42",
  organizationId: "org_7",
  roles: role,
});
console.log(token);
```

## 9. Run and sign tokens [#9-run-and-sign-tokens]

Start the server in one terminal:

```sh
bun run dev
```

You should see the `listening` line:

```text
my-app listening on http://localhost:8000
```

In a second terminal, sign a member token and an admin token and store them in shell variables:

```sh
MEMBER=$(bun run scripts/issue-token.ts)
ADMIN=$(bun run scripts/issue-token.ts admin)
```

Each command prints a token starting with `eyJ`. The tokens are valid for one hour.

## 10. Call the protected actions [#10-call-the-protected-actions]

Request the profile without a token:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"account","action":"profile","payload":{"includeOrganization":true}}'
```

You should see HTTP 400 and the verifier's message:

```json
{"status":false,"message":"No JWT token found in header","data":{}}
```

Request the profile with the member token:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MEMBER" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"account","action":"profile","payload":{"includeOrganization":true}}'
```

You should see HTTP 200 with the identity from the token:

```json
{"status":true,"message":"Action 'account.profile' executed","data":{"profile":{"userId":"user_42","organizationId":"org_7"}}}
```

Request the audit action with the member token. The role hook refuses it:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MEMBER" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"account","action":"audit","payload":{}}'
```

You should see `Access denied` in the message. The status is HTTP 400, because Nile Js reports action failures with 400:

```json
{"status":false,"message":"Access denied","data":{}}
```

Request the same action with the admin token:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"account","action":"audit","payload":{}}'
```

You should see HTTP 200 and the audit entries:

```json
{"status":true,"message":"Action 'account.audit' executed","data":{"entries":[{"event":"profile.viewed","at":"2026-10-23T09:00:00.000Z"}]}}
```

Public actions still work without a token. The starter's `tasks.list` returns HTTP 200 whether or not you send one.

## 11. Type-check [#11-type-check]

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

You should see no output and exit with status 0.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **`JWT_SECRET must be set to at least 32 characters`.** The server did not find `.env`, or the value is shorter than 32 characters. Check the file location and restart `bun run dev`.
- **`JWT authentication failed: invalid token`.** The token is malformed or was signed with a different secret. Sign a new token after changing `JWT_SECRET`.

- **`JWT authentication failed: token expired`.** The token's `exp` time has passed. Sign a new token.
- **The admin token is still refused.** The token lacks the `admin` role. Sign it with `bun run scripts/issue-token.ts admin`.

A failed JWT message names the reason only, such as `token expired`, and never contains the token, so it is safe to log.

## See also [#see-also]

- [Authentication and hooks](/guide/features/authentication-and-hooks) explains each option used here.
- [Authentication](/guide/basics/auth) covers the session fields and external providers.
- [Realtime order updates](/guide/examples/realtime-orders) applies the same token check to a socket connection.


---

# Rate-limited quote

This example adds a public `catalog.quote` action with a token-bucket limit. Each client may send a burst of 20 requests, and the bucket refills at 5 requests per second. A client that exceeds the limit gets a failure that says how long to wait.

## What you need [#what-you-need]

- The starter project from the [examples overview](/guide/examples), installed with `bun install`.

## 1. Write the public action [#1-write-the-public-action]

Create `src/services/catalog/actions/quote.ts`. It is not protected, so anyone who can reach the server can call it. The limit is what protects it:

```ts
import { createAction } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Err, Ok } from "slang-ts";
import { z } from "zod";

const quoteSchema = z.object({
  sku: z.string().trim().min(1, "SKU is required"),
  quantity: z.number().int().min(1, "Quantity must be at least 1").max(10, "Quantity cannot exceed 10"),
});

type QuoteInput = z.infer<typeof quoteSchema>;

const PRICE_IN_CENTS: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {
  "TSHIRT-BLUE": 1500,
  "MUG-WHITE": 900,
};

const quoteHandler = (input: QuoteInput) => {
  const unitPrice = PRICE_IN_CENTS[input.sku];
  if (unitPrice === undefined) {
    return Err("Unknown SKU");
  }

  return Ok({
    sku: input.sku,
    quantity: input.quantity,
    totalInCents: unitPrice * input.quantity,
  });
};

export const quoteAction = createAction<QuoteInput>({
  name: "quote",
  description: "Return the public price for a product quantity",
  validation: quoteSchema,
  handler: quoteHandler,
});
```

## 2. Register the service [#2-register-the-service]

Replace `src/services/services.config.ts` so the `catalog` service is registered next to `tasks`:

```ts
import { createServices, type Services } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { quoteAction } from "./catalog/actions/quote";
import { createTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/create";
import { deleteTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/delete";
import { getTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/get";
import { listTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/list";
import { updateTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/update";

export const services: Services = createServices([
  {
    name: "tasks",
    description: "Task management with CRUD operations",
    meta: { version: "1.0.0" },
    actions: [
      createTaskAction,
      listTaskAction,
      getTaskAction,
      updateTaskAction,
      deleteTaskAction,
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "catalog",
    description: "Public product information",
    actions: [quoteAction],
  },
]);
```

## 3. Add the limiter [#3-add-the-limiter]

Replace `src/index.ts`. The `execution.rateLimit` policy applies to every action. Its key is the client's address, which Nile Js provides in `context.clientKey`:

```ts
import { createLogger, createNileServer, utils } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { Ok, safeTry } from "slang-ts";
import { db } from "@/db/client";
import { services } from "@/services/services.config";

const logger = createLogger("my-app", {
  mode: "dev",
  chunking: "monthly",
});

/** Token bucket: a burst of 20 quotes per client, refilled at 5 per second. */
const quoteLimiter = utils.createRateLimiter({
  strategy: "token-bucket",
  capacity: 20,
  refillPerSecond: 5,
  maxKeys: 10_000,
});

/** Push schema to PGLite on boot */
const pushSchema = async () => {
  const result = await safeTry(() =>
    db.execute(sql`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
        id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        title TEXT NOT NULL,
        description TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
        created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
      )
    `)
  );

  if (result.isErr) {
    console.error("[pushSchema] Failed:", result.error);
  }
};

const server = await createNileServer({
  serverName: "my-app",
  runtime: "bun",
  native: true,
  project: { structure: "error" },
  services,
  resources: { logger, database: db },
  execution: {
    rateLimit: {
      store: quoteLimiter,
      key: ({ context }) => context.clientKey ?? "anonymous",
    },
  },
  rest: {
    baseUrl: "/api",
    host: "localhost",
    port: 8000,
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8000"],
    enableStatus: true,
    discovery: { enabled: true },
  },
  onBoot: {
    // The first PGlite start on a slow machine can take longer than the 10 second default.
    maxWaitTime: 30_000,
    fn: async (ctx) => {
      await pushSchema();
      ctx.resources?.logger?.info({
        atFunction: "onBoot",
        message: "my-app booted - PGLite schema ready",
      });
      return Ok(null);
    },
  },
});

if (server.nativeRest) {
  const port = server.config.rest?.port ?? 8000;
  Bun.serve({ port, fetch: server.nativeRest.fetch });
  console.log(`\nmy-app listening on http://localhost:${port}\n`);
}
```

## 4. Run the server [#4-run-the-server]

```sh
bun run dev
```

You should see the `listening` line:

```text
my-app listening on http://localhost:8000
```

## 5. Send a burst [#5-send-a-burst]

In a second terminal, send 25 requests in a row and print each HTTP status:

```sh
for i in $(seq 1 25); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"catalog","action":"quote","payload":{"sku":"MUG-WHITE","quantity":2}}'
done
echo
```

You should see 21 `200` responses followed by 4 `400` responses. The exact split depends on timing, because the bucket refills while the loop runs:

```text
200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 200 400 400 400 400
```

## 6. Read the refusal [#6-read-the-refusal]

The first refused request returns:

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded; retry after 147ms",
  "data": {}
}
```

The number changes between runs. Wait for the time shown, then send another request. A request after the wait returns the quote:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/services \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"intent":"execute","service":"catalog","action":"quote","payload":{"sku":"TSHIRT-BLUE","quantity":3}}'
```

You should see HTTP 200 and the total in cents:

```json
{"status":true,"message":"Action 'catalog.quote' executed","data":{"sku":"TSHIRT-BLUE","quantity":3,"totalInCents":4500}}
```

## 7. Type-check [#7-type-check]

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

You should see no output and exit with status 0.

## Limits in this example [#limits-in-this-example]

- The limiter keeps its counts in this process. Two replicas each allow a full burst.
- Restarting the server resets every client's bucket.
- Every client behind one proxy may share one address. Configure the server's client address resolution before you rely on per-client limits in production.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **Every request is refused right away.** The earlier loop used up the bucket. Wait a few seconds and try again.
- **`Unknown SKU`.** Use `MUG-WHITE` or `TSHIRT-BLUE`, the two SKUs in the handler's price table.

## See also [#see-also]

- [Rate limiting](/guide/features/rate-limiting) explains the strategies, policy layers and the HTTP-level limit.
- [Execution options](/guide/advanced/execution-options) shows per-service and per-action policies.
- [Production operations](/guide/reference/operations) covers client addresses behind proxies.


---

# Realtime order updates

This example connects a socket client to an order topic. A protected action changes an order's status and publishes the change to subscribers in the same organization. A client from another organization can neither subscribe to that topic nor change the order.

## What you need [#what-you-need]

- The starter project from the [examples overview](/guide/examples), installed with `bun install`.
- The same token helper and secret setup as [the protected profile example](/guide/examples/protected-profile). The steps below repeat the parts you need.

## 1. Add the packages [#1-add-the-packages]

```sh
bun add @nilejs/client hono
```

## 2. Add the secret [#2-add-the-secret]

Create `.env` in the project root:

```text
JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-string-of-at-least-32-characters
```

## 3. Read the secret in one place [#3-read-the-secret-in-one-place]

Create `src/config.ts`:

```ts
const jwtSecret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;

if (jwtSecret === undefined || jwtSecret.length < 32) {
  throw new Error("JWT_SECRET must be set to at least 32 characters");
}

export const config = {
  jwtSecret: jwtSecret,
};
```

## 4. Define the topic [#4-define-the-topic]

Create `src/realtime/topics.ts`. The topic has a payload schema and a scope schema. Subscribers match on `organizationId`:

```ts
import { createTopics, type InferTopics } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { z } from "zod";

export const topics = createTopics({
  "orders.updated": {
    schema: z.object({
      orderId: z.string(),
      status: z.enum(["placed", "packed", "shipped"]),
    }),
    scope: z.object({
      organizationId: z.string(),
    }),
  },
});

export type Topics = InferTopics<typeof topics>;
```

## 5. Verify the token on each connection [#5-verify-the-token-on-each-connection]

Create `src/realtime/socket-auth.ts`. The socket client sends its token in the connection's `auth` object. This function runs `verifyJWT` on it and returns the identity and the headers that protected actions need:

```ts
import { type AuthConfig, verifyJWT, type WebSocketIdentity } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Err, Ok, type Result } from "slang-ts";
import { config } from "@/config";

const jwtConfig: AuthConfig = {
  secret: config.jwtSecret,
  method: "header",
};

/** The socket client sends its token in the connection auth object. */
export const authenticateSocket = async (
  _request: Request,
  auth: Record<string, string>
): Promise<Result<WebSocketIdentity, string>> => {
  const bearer = `Bearer ${auth.token ?? ""}`;
  const headers = new Headers({ authorization: bearer });

  const verified = await verifyJWT({ headers: headers }, jwtConfig);
  if (verified.isErr) {
    return Err(verified.error);
  }

  return Ok({
    session: {
      userId: verified.value.userId,
      organizationId: verified.value.organizationId,
    },
    credentials: { headers: headers },
  });
};
```

## 6. Keep the orders in memory [#6-keep-the-orders-in-memory]

Create `src/services/orders/store.ts`. It holds one seeded order for `org_7`. A restart resets it, which is fine for this example:

```ts
export type OrderStatus = "placed" | "packed" | "shipped";

export interface Order {
  id: string;
  organizationId: string;
  status: OrderStatus;
}

/** Process-local storage for this example. Restarting the server resets it. */
const orders = new Map<string, Order>([
  ["ord_1001", { id: "ord_1001", organizationId: "org_7", status: "placed" }],
]);

export const findOrder = (orderId: string): Order | undefined => {
  return orders.get(orderId);
};

export const updateOrderStatus = (
  orderId: string,
  status: OrderStatus
): Order | undefined => {
  const existing = orders.get(orderId);
  if (existing === undefined) {
    return undefined;
  }

  const updated: Order = { ...existing, status: status };
  orders.set(orderId, updated);
  return updated;
};
```

## 7. Add the protected status action [#7-add-the-protected-status-action]

Create `src/services/orders/actions/set-status.ts`. The action checks that the order belongs to the caller's organization, updates the status and publishes to the topic with `getContext({ topics })`:

```ts
import { createAction, type NileContext, getContext } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { Err, Ok } from "slang-ts";
import { z } from "zod";
import { topics } from "@/realtime/topics";
import { findOrder, updateOrderStatus } from "@/services/orders/store";

const setStatusSchema = z.object({
  orderId: z.string().min(1, "Order ID is required"),
  status: z.enum(["placed", "packed", "shipped"]),
});

type SetStatusInput = z.infer<typeof setStatusSchema>;

const setStatusHandler = async (
  input: SetStatusInput,
  context?: NileContext<unknown>
) => {
  const session = context?.getSession("rest");
  if (session === undefined) {
    return Err("Sign in to continue");
  }

  const existing = findOrder(input.orderId);
  if (existing === undefined || existing.organizationId !== session.organizationId) {
    return Err("Order not found");
  }

  const order = updateOrderStatus(input.orderId, input.status);
  if (order === undefined) {
    return Err("Order not found");
  }

  const { websocket } = getContext({ topics: topics });
  const sent = await websocket.send({
    topic: "orders.updated",
    scope: { organizationId: order.organizationId },
    data: { orderId: order.id, status: order.status },
  });

  if (sent.isErr) {
    return Err(sent.error);
  }

  return Ok({ order: order });
};

export const setStatusAction = createAction<SetStatusInput>({
  name: "set-status",
  description: "Change an order status and notify subscribers",
  isProtected: true,
  validation: setStatusSchema,
  handler: setStatusHandler,
});
```

## 8. Register the service [#8-register-the-service]

Replace `src/services/services.config.ts` so the `orders` service is registered:

```ts
import { createServices, type Services } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { setStatusAction } from "./orders/actions/set-status";
import { createTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/create";
import { deleteTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/delete";
import { getTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/get";
import { listTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/list";
import { updateTaskAction } from "./tasks/actions/update";

export const services: Services = createServices([
  {
    name: "tasks",
    description: "Task management with CRUD operations",
    meta: { version: "1.0.0" },
    actions: [
      createTaskAction,
      listTaskAction,
      getTaskAction,
      updateTaskAction,
      deleteTaskAction,
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "orders",
    description: "Order status changes",
    actions: [setStatusAction],
  },
]);
```

## 9. Configure the server [#9-configure-the-server]

Replace `src/index.ts`. It adds the `websocket` block, which uses the topics and the policies, and serves the HTTP and socket handlers with `Bun.serve`:

```ts
import { createLogger, createNileServer } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { Ok, safeTry } from "slang-ts";
import { config } from "@/config";
import { db } from "@/db/client";
import { authenticateSocket } from "@/realtime/socket-auth";
import { topics } from "@/realtime/topics";
import { services } from "@/services/services.config";

const logger = createLogger("my-app", {
  mode: "dev",
  chunking: "monthly",
});

/** Push schema to PGLite on boot */
const pushSchema = async () => {
  const result = await safeTry(() =>
    db.execute(sql`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
        id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        title TEXT NOT NULL,
        description TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
        created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
      )
    `)
  );

  if (result.isErr) {
    console.error("[pushSchema] Failed:", result.error);
  }
};

const server = await createNileServer({
  serverName: "my-app",
  runtime: "bun",
  native: true,
  project: { structure: "error" },
  services,
  resources: { logger, database: db },
  auth: { secret: config.jwtSecret, method: "header" },
  websocket: {
    topics: topics,
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:5173"],
    authenticate: authenticateSocket,
    authorizeSubscription: ({ scope, identity }) => {
      return Ok(scope.organizationId === identity.session?.organizationId);
    },
    authorizePublish: () => Ok(false),
  },
  rest: {
    baseUrl: "/api",
    host: "localhost",
    port: 8000,
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:5173"],
    enableStatus: true,
    discovery: { enabled: true },
  },
  onBoot: {
    // The first PGlite start on a slow machine can take longer than the 10 second default.
    maxWaitTime: 30_000,
    fn: async (ctx) => {
      await pushSchema();
      ctx.resources?.logger?.info({
        atFunction: "onBoot",
        message: "my-app booted - PGLite schema ready",
      });
      return Ok(null);
    },
  },
});

const websocketBun = server.websocket?.bun;
if (websocketBun === undefined) {
  throw new Error("Bun socket adapter is unavailable");
}

const listener = Bun.serve({
  port: 8000,
  fetch: server.fetch,
  websocket: websocketBun,
  idleTimeout: server.websocket?.idleTimeout,
});

server.lifecycle.register({
  name: "http-listener",
  stop: () => {
    listener.stop(false);
  },
});

console.log(`\nmy-app listening on http://localhost:${listener.port}\n`);
```

`authorizePublish` returns `Ok(false)`, so clients cannot publish to the topic. Only server code sends messages.

## 10. Add the token helper [#10-add-the-token-helper]

Create `scripts/issue-token.ts`. Pass an organization ID as the first argument:

```ts
import { sign } from "hono/jwt";
import { config } from "../src/config";

const ONE_HOUR_IN_SECONDS = 60 * 60;

/** Development helper: prints a signed token for an organization. */
const organizationId = process.argv[2] ?? "org_7";
const expiresAt = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + ONE_HOUR_IN_SECONDS;

const token = await sign(
  {
    userId: "user_42",
    organizationId: organizationId,
    exp: expiresAt,
  },
  config.jwtSecret
);

console.log(token);
```

## 11. Write the socket client [#11-write-the-socket-client]

Create `client-orders.ts`. It subscribes to `org_7`, calls `set-status` over the same socket connection and waits for the live message:

```ts
import { createNileSocketClient } from "@nilejs/client";
import type { Topics } from "./src/realtime/topics";

interface OrderActions {
  orders: {
    "set-status": { orderId: string; status: "placed" | "packed" | "shipped" };
  };
}

const token = process.env.TOKEN ?? "";

const socket = createNileSocketClient<OrderActions, Topics>({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:8000",
  auth: () => ({ token: token }),
});

const messageReceived = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
  const subscribed = socket.receive({
    topic: "orders.updated",
    scope: { organizationId: "org_7" },
    onMessage: (message) => {
      console.log("live update", message.data.orderId, message.data.status);
      resolve();
    },
  });

  void subscribed.then((result) => {
    if (result.isErr) {
      console.error("subscribe failed", result.error);
      resolve();
    }
  });
});

await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
  setTimeout(resolve, 500);
});

const changed = await socket.invoke({
  service: "orders",
  action: "set-status",
  payload: { orderId: "ord_1001", status: "packed" },
});

if (changed.isErr) {
  console.error("invoke failed", changed.error, changed.details);
} else {
  console.log("invoke ok", JSON.stringify(changed.value));
}

await messageReceived;
socket.close();
```

## 12. Run it [#12-run-it]

Start the server in one terminal:

```sh
bun run dev
```

In a second terminal, run the client with a token for `org_7`:

```sh
TOKEN=$(bun run scripts/issue-token.ts org_7) bun run client-orders.ts
```

You should see the live message and the invoke result:

```text
live update ord_1001 packed
invoke ok {"order":{"id":"ord_1001","organizationId":"org_7","status":"packed"}}
```

Now run it with a token for `org_8`, which belongs to another organization:

```sh
TOKEN=$(bun run scripts/issue-token.ts org_8) bun run client-orders.ts
```

You should see the subscription refused and the order reported as not found for this organization. No live message arrives:

```text
subscribe failed Topic access denied
invoke failed Order not found null
```

A client that sends no token cannot connect at all. Its socket attempt fails at authentication with `Socket connection failed`.

## 13. Type-check [#13-type-check]

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

You should see no output and exit with status 0.

## Limits in this example [#limits-in-this-example]

- The order store is a `Map` in this process. A second server instance would have its own orders.
- Subscribers in other processes do not receive messages sent by this one. Connect a shared message bus before you run several replicas.
- The live message is not stored. A client that reconnects should reload the order with a normal action.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **`Socket connection failed`.** The token is missing, expired or signed with another secret. Sign a new token with the same `.env`.
- **The client connects but receives nothing.** Check that the subscription's `organizationId` matches the token and the order. Watch `subscribe failed` in the output.
- **`Bun socket adapter is unavailable`.** The server did not start with `runtime: "bun"` and `native: true`. Check `src/index.ts`.

## See also [#see-also]

- [WebSockets](/guide/features/websockets) explains each policy and limit.
- [Sockets and typed messages](/guide/reference/realtime) has the complete contract.
- [Protected profile](/guide/examples/protected-profile) explains the JWT check this example reuses.


---

# Tasks API in React

This example connects a React task list to the starter's `tasks` service. The component loads tasks, adds a new task through `@nilejs/client` and shows the validation message when the title is empty. You will build it in an existing starter project and check it from the command line, then mount the component in your React app.

## What you need [#what-you-need]

- The starter project from the [examples overview](/guide/examples), installed with `bun install`.
- A React app that will render the component. A Vite app on port 5173 works with the origin setting below.

## 1. Add the frontend packages [#1-add-the-frontend-packages]

```sh
bun add @nilejs/client react react-dom
bun add -d @types/react @types/react-dom
```

You should see both commands finish with a line such as `installed react@19` and no errors.

## 2. Allow the React app's origin [#2-allow-the-react-apps-origin]

Browsers block responses from another origin unless the server lists it. Replace `src/index.ts` with this file. It adds `http://localhost:5173` to `rest.allowedOrigins`. Everything else is the starter's setup.

```ts
import { createLogger, createNileServer } from "@nilejs/nile";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { Ok, safeTry } from "slang-ts";
import { db } from "@/db/client";
import { services } from "@/services/services.config";

const logger = createLogger("my-app", {
  mode: "dev",
  chunking: "monthly",
});

/** Push schema to PGLite on boot */
const pushSchema = async () => {
  const result = await safeTry(() =>
    db.execute(sql`
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
        id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
        title TEXT NOT NULL,
        description TEXT,
        status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
        created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
        updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
      )
    `)
  );

  if (result.isErr) {
    console.error("[pushSchema] Failed:", result.error);
  }
};

const server = await createNileServer({
  serverName: "my-app",
  runtime: "bun",
  native: true,
  project: { structure: "error" },
  services,
  resources: { logger, database: db },
  rest: {
    baseUrl: "/api",
    host: "localhost",
    port: 8000,
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8000", "http://localhost:5173"],
    enableStatus: true,
    discovery: { enabled: true },
  },
  onBoot: {
    // The first PGlite start on a slow machine can take longer than the 10 second default.
    maxWaitTime: 30_000,
    fn: async (ctx) => {
      await pushSchema();
      ctx.resources?.logger?.info({
        atFunction: "onBoot",
        message: "my-app booted - PGLite schema ready",
      });
      return Ok(null);
    },
  },
});

// Register custom middleware (runs before all service requests)
server.nativeRest?.addMiddleware("/api", async (c, next) => {
  const start = performance.now();
  await next();
  const ms = (performance.now() - start).toFixed(1);
  logger.info({
    atFunction: "requestLog",
    message: `${c.request.method} ${c.path} - ${ms}ms`,
  });
  return undefined;
});

if (server.nativeRest) {
  const port = server.config.rest?.port ?? 8000;
  Bun.serve({ port, fetch: server.nativeRest.fetch });
  console.log(`\nmy-app listening on http://localhost:${port}\n`);
}
```

## 3. Let TypeScript check the React files [#3-let-typescript-check-the-react-files]

Replace `tsconfig.json` so the compiler reads `.tsx` files and uses the React JSX transform:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ESNext",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": ".",
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./src/*"]
    }
  },
  "include": ["./src/**/*.ts", "./src/**/*.tsx", "./client-check.ts", "./drizzle.config.ts"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "data"]
}
```

## 4. Write the typed client [#4-write-the-typed-client]

Create `src/web/nile-client.ts`. The payload map gives each action a type, and the zod schemas check the response before the component uses it:

```ts
import { createNileClient } from "@nilejs/client";
import { Err, Ok, type Result } from "slang-ts";
import { z } from "zod";

export interface TaskPayloads {
  tasks: {
    list: Record<string, never>;
    create: { title: string; description?: string };
    complete: { id: string };
  };
}

export const taskSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string(),
  status: z.enum(["pending", "in-progress", "done"]),
  created_at: z.string(),
  updated_at: z.string(),
});

export type Task = z.infer<typeof taskSchema>;

const taskListSchema = z.object({
  tasks: z.array(taskSchema),
});

const taskResponseSchema = z.object({
  task: taskSchema,
});

export const nile = createNileClient<TaskPayloads>({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:8000/api",
});

export const loadTasks = async (): Promise<Result<Task[], string>> => {
  const listed = await nile.invoke({
    service: "tasks",
    action: "list",
    payload: {},
  });

  if (listed.isErr) {
    return Err(listed.error);
  }

  const parsed = taskListSchema.safeParse(listed.value);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return Err("Unexpected response from tasks.list");
  }

  return Ok(parsed.data.tasks);
};

export const createTask = async (
  title: string
): Promise<Result<Task, string>> => {
  const created = await nile.invoke({
    service: "tasks",
    action: "create",
    payload: { title: title },
  });

  if (created.isErr) {
    return Err(created.error);
  }

  const parsed = taskResponseSchema.safeParse(created.value);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return Err("Unexpected response from tasks.create");
  }

  return Ok(parsed.data.task);
};
```

Each function returns a Result from `slang-ts`. Callers check `isErr` first, then read `value`.

## 5. Write the component [#5-write-the-component]

Create `src/web/task-board.tsx`. It loads tasks once, submits the form through `createTask` and shows any failure in a status line:

```tsx
import { type FormEvent, type ReactElement, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { createTask, loadTasks, type Task } from "./nile-client";

export const TaskBoard = (): ReactElement => {
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[]>([]);
  const [title, setTitle] = useState<string>("");
  const [message, setMessage] = useState<string>("Loading tasks...");

  useEffect(() => {
    const load = async (): Promise<void> => {
      const loaded = await loadTasks();
      if (loaded.isErr) {
        setMessage(loaded.error);
        return;
      }
      setTasks(loaded.value);
      setMessage("");
    };

    void load();
  }, []);

  const handleSubmit = async (event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>): Promise<void> => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const created = await createTask(title);
    if (created.isErr) {
      setMessage(created.error);
      return;
    }
    setTasks((current: Task[]) => [...current, created.value]);
    setTitle("");
    setMessage("");
  };

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Tasks</h1>
      <form
        onSubmit={(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
          void handleSubmit(event);
        }}
      >
        <label htmlFor="task-title">Title</label>
        <input
          id="task-title"
          value={title}
          onChange={(event) => {
            setTitle(event.target.value);
          }}
        />
        <button type="submit">Add task</button>
      </form>
      {message === "" ? null : <p role="status">{message}</p>}
      <ul>
        {tasks.map((task: Task) => (
          <li key={task.id}>
            {task.title} ({task.status})
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </main>
  );
};
```

Mount it from the entry point of your React app, for example:

```tsx
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { TaskBoard } from "./web/task-board";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root") as HTMLElement).render(<TaskBoard />);
```

## 6. Check the calls from the command line [#6-check-the-calls-from-the-command-line]

Create `client-check.ts` in the project root. It runs the same functions the component uses, without a browser:

```ts
import { createTask, loadTasks } from "./src/web/nile-client";

const runClientCheck = async (): Promise<void> => {
  const created = await createTask("Written from the React example");
  if (created.isErr) {
    console.error(created.error);
    return;
  }
  console.log("created", created.value.id, created.value.status);

  const listed = await loadTasks();
  if (listed.isErr) {
    console.error(listed.error);
    return;
  }
  console.log("listed", listed.value.length, "tasks");

  const rejected = await createTask("");
  console.log("empty title rejected", rejected.isErr, rejected.isErr ? rejected.error : "");
};

await runClientCheck();
```

Start the server in one terminal:

```sh
bun run dev
```

In a second terminal, run the check:

```sh
bun run client-check.ts
```

You should see something like this. IDs and the task count change between runs:

```text
created 3f5ac4b5-d128-4dd4-812e-7805a8640909 pending
listed 2 tasks
empty title rejected true Validation failed: ✖ Title is required
  → at title
```

The last line proves the server's validation reached the client. Because the client returns `isErr`, the component can show the message without catching an exception.

## 7. Check the types and the server render [#7-check-the-types-and-the-server-render]

```sh
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

You should see no output and the command exits with status 0.

To confirm that the component renders on the server without a browser, create `render-check.tsx` with this content and run it with Bun:

```tsx
import { renderToString } from "react-dom/server";
import { TaskBoard } from "./src/web/task-board";

console.log(renderToString(<TaskBoard />));
```

```sh
bun run render-check.tsx
```

You should see the first render, before the effect loads tasks:

```text
<main><h1>Tasks</h1><form><label for="task-title">Title</label><input id="task-title" value=""/><button type="submit">Add task</button></form><p role="status">Loading tasks...</p><ul></ul></main>
```

In the browser, the same component loads the list when it mounts. This guide checked the client and the render on the server; check the browser step in your own app.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **`No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header` in the browser.** The React app's origin is missing from `rest.allowedOrigins`. Add it, save `src/index.ts`, and reload.
- **The list shows `Loading tasks...` forever.** The server is not running, or `baseUrl` points at another port. Check the terminal running `bun run dev`.
- **`Unexpected response from tasks.list`.** The response shape changed. Compare it with the `taskSchema` in `nile-client.ts`.

## See also [#see-also]

- [Frontend client](/guide/basics/client) explains request options and the Result shape.
- [Errors and Results](/guide/basics/errors-and-results) covers the three response shapes.
- [Validation and errors](/guide/features/validation-and-errors) explains the `details.issues` field for forms.
